clue.text: A country taking a boy from the East, he being in exile

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the East means reading right to left, so the whole run is turned round

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A nation adopts a lad from abroad, the youngster an exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns AMALIALAD (A, MALI, A, LAD) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan spiritual leader has lived in exile in India since 1959, so he is the man described.

clue.text: 7's faith threatened distressed 12

definitions.note: the clue at 7 is the author, so 7's means a work of his, a noun phrase like the title

indicators.note: something distressed is knocked about and battered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
twelve o'clock is noon

explanation.surface: A believer's faith is menaced, leaving a damsel in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: The '12' looks like a pointer to 12-across, DAMSEL, but it is simply the number twelve: midday. 'distressed' rearranges FAITH, THREATENED and NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1932 non-fiction book about bullfighting is by Ernest Hemingway, the author at 7, so it is one of his.

clue.text: No good stuffing pancakes without topping, these on the inside

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so the abbreviation is packed into the trimmed pancakes
in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: blinis are small Russian buckwheat pancakes

explanation.surface: Pancakes without any topping are no good, though the filling is inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without topping' cuts the B from BLINIS to leave LINIS, and 'stuffing' puts NG into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Linings are the layers of material fitted on the inner side of a garment or container.

clue.text: See 1
Drink fizzy cola — what might bubbles do?

indicators.note: a fizzy drink is agitated and bubbling, signalling that these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
bubbles pop when they burst

explanation.surface: A fizzy cola is poured and the bubbles burst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' turns COLA into ALCO.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy, ready-mixed alcoholic beverage sold in bottles.

clue.text: See 1
Part of London that's extremely sexy, detailed

parts.note: so means extremely, as in so good

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: A district of London famed for being extremely raunchy, described in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an ends-only signal on 'sexy' but simply means SO; 'detailed' cuts HOT to HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in London's West End long known for its nightlife and sex shops.

clue.text: Caught in shoe, might this trip dignitary up?

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits within the footwear word

parts.note: a sandal is a kind of shoe
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a shoe wonders whether this could make an important figure stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: A scandal is a figurative trip-up for a dignitary, which fits the shoe image of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a disgrace that can bring down, or trip up, a public figure.

clue.text: Confine wife in the clutches of merry author …

parts.note: to hem in is to confine

indicators.note: something held in another's clutches is gripped inside it, so the abbreviation goes within the word for merry

parts.note: gay in its old sense means merry

explanation.surface: Keep a wife held tight by a cheerful writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the clutches of' puts W inside GAY. The ellipsis carries the sentence on into 13-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American novelist who wrote war and bullfighting stories.

clue.text: Attractive catch in wizard

indicators.note: the word for catch sits inside the word for wizard

parts.note: wizard and magic are both informal British words for excellent
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A captivating trick performed by a sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wizard' reads as a sorcerer but here is old British slang for excellent, as is 'magic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic describes something that pulls things towards it, literally or by charm.

clue.text: See 13
New chapter in For Whom The Bell Tolls, taken from there

indicators.note: the two abbreviations are placed inside the word supplied by the title

parts.note: John Donne's line runs 'never send to know for whom the bell tolls; it tolls for thee'

explanation.surface: A fresh chapter added to Hemingway's novel, quoted from there.
explanation.walkthrough: The title, another Hemingway novel, stands for its answer in Donne's sermon: thee. 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thence is an old adverb meaning from that place.

clue.text: Showing example, shortly, round back of design

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round the single letter, enclosing it
shortly signals the word cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a paradigm is a typical example or model

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Displaying a model in brief around the end of a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims PARADIGM to PARADIG, which goes 'round' N, the end of 'design'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parading is putting on show, as in parading one's knowledge.

clue.text: Naughty males after daughter, finding girl

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the abbreviation
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Badly behaved men chase someone's daughter and find a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges MALES as AMSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old or literary word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: … whose distant source of milk left empty, filling rotten molars

definitions.note: following 7, it means a book whose author is Hemingway

parts.note: afar means at a distance
a ewe is a female sheep giving milk

indicators.note: a filling goes into a tooth, so these letters are put inside the shuffled teeth
rotten teeth are decayed, signalling the letters are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, keeping only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the author's sentence: his remote dairy animal departed, the gap filled in decaying back teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on from 7: the author whose book this is. 'rotten' makes LOARMS, and 'filling' and 'empty' set the ends of 'left' just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1929 novel of the Italian front is by Ernest Hemingway, so it is one of his works.

clue.text: Lithium compound soluble, potentially damaging

parts.note: Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

indicators.note: a chemical compound mixes elements, so the letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lithium salt that dissolves may be hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' rearranges SOLUBLE as BELLOUS. The chemistry surface hides a legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Libellous writing is defamatory, and so can harm a person's reputation.

clue.text: Hands holding nothing, nothing with both hands? These passed for support

indicators.note: the outer word grips the pieces inside it

parts.note: paws is informal for hands
O is zero, nothing
O again is zero
R and L are right and left, a hand each

explanation.surface: Empty-handed people receive nothing at all, though these acts were meant to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Laws were English laws, from Tudor times to 1948, for relief of the poor; 'holding' puts the noughts and both hands after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Laws were statutes enacted to provide relief for the destitute in England.

clue.text: Screwed up as rubbish, in the middle I went — here!

definitions.text: Screwed up as rubbish, in the middle I went — here!

indicators.note: screwed-up paper is crumpled, so the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the central letter of the word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crumpled up as trash, I landed right in the centre of this receptacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed up' rearranges AS, B (the middle letter of 'rubbish') and IWENT. Read as a whole, the clue describes balled-up rubbish thrown into a bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastebin is a container for rubbish, the destination for crumpled waste paper.

clue.text: Organisational process, it's rising and falling

indicators.note: in a down clue rising reads upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: the word it, with 's as a link
dying, as soldiers fall in battle

explanation.surface: Something ordered that goes up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidying is putting things in order, a process of organising.

clue.text: One entering African country with different capital — finding another?

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the altered country name
capital here means first letter, which is swapped for another

parts.note: Zambia is a country in southern Africa
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in an African nation that has a new capital city, and finds another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with different capital' swaps Z for N, giving NAMBIA, and 'entering' puts I in after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is another African country, west of its neighbour in the clue.

clue.text: A painter passing northern city in the East

indicators.note: the painter's group goes past the abbreviation, following it

parts.note: Goya was a Spanish painter

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter travels beyond a northern city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' places A GOYA after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagoya is a large Japanese city, so a city in the Far East.

clue.text: Work at first of suspects, say, up for interrogating people

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the whole run is turned

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: eg (for example) is said before an instance

explanation.surface: Getting to work first on the suspects, perhaps up for questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OPATSEG backwards. The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo were the Nazi secret police, notorious for brutal questioning.

clue.text: Swinger missing overture from opera after 1 down 3 5

indicators.note: the light at 3 is 'in', so it acts as a containment signal

parts.note: the light at 5 is afternoon, PM

indicators.note: the trimmed opera follows the word for death

parts.note: the light at 1 is death, which is an end

indicators.note: the overture is the opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Lulu is an opera by Alban Berg

explanation.surface: A swinging thing goes without the opening of an opera after an afternoon death.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1, 3 and 5 as DEATH IN AFTERNOON: END and ULU (LULU less its first letter, 'missing overture from') go 'in' PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro, as in a clock.

clue.text: Ship in a bottle, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a bottle is one kind of container for liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the surface conjures the hobby of building model ships in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessel means both a boat and any hollow container for holding liquid.

clue.text: Sculpture perhaps alternatively titled 13 9?

parts.note: the famous Greek statue has lost both its arms, so Hemingway's title of leave-taking from arms would suit it

explanation.walkthrough: The statue is armless, hence its joke title A FAREWELL TO ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Greek marble statue of Aphrodite in the Louvre is missing both arms.

clue.text: Writer leaves girl to run away with another

indicators.note: the writing tool departs from the name, removed from it

parts.note: Penelope is a girl's name
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An author walks out on a young woman, who runs off with another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author, but is the PEN that 'leaves' PENELOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly with a lover to marry.

clue.text: See 22
26 a modest residence

parts.note: the light at 26 is plug, which is a bung
low means humble, modest

explanation.surface: A small, unassuming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 refers to the answer at 26-across, a synonym of bung.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a single-storey house, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Advertisement as filler

definitions.meaning: a promotional mention of a product
a stopper that fills a hole

explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is both a publicity mention and a stopper for blocking a hole.

clue.text: Mineral which may bend teaspoons

indicators.note: bending distorts a shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stone that can twist cutlery, like a spoon-bender's trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may bend' rearranges TEASPOONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapstone is a soft rock made largely of talc, a mineral.
